description: Kern County’s Senior Information and Referral Program helps seniors and their families identify local services, including care, meals, transportation and legal resources.
introduction: Kern County’s Senior Information and Referral Program helps seniors and their families identify local services, including care, meals, transportation and legal resources.

who: Seniors and families seeking resources can contact the program. Each referred service has its own eligibility requirements. Information and referral cannot be denied because a person does not contribute.
sections.get: Staff offer resource listings, referrals and help with various forms. Ask about in-home care, meal services, transportation or other needs rather than assuming one referral covers everything.
sections.docs: Write down the person’s location, main needs and any urgent safety concern. Ask the referred provider about documents and intake; referral staff do not automatically enroll you in every program.
sections.apply: Call 661-868-1000 or 800-510-2020. The program page lists the office at 5357 Truxtun Avenue, Bakersfield.
sections.after: Record provider contacts and follow up directly. Ask for alternatives if an agency cannot serve you. For ongoing care, clarify costs and what the provider can actually deliver before agreeing.
sections.sources:
• Kern senior information and referral
  • USA Assistance background and screenshots

faqs: Can a family member ask for resources?
Yes. The program describes assisting seniors and their families.
Must I donate to receive a referral?
No. The page says referrals are not denied for failure to contribute.
Can staff explain in-home care options?
The program provides referrals to home services and other care resources.
No. The receiving service determines its own requirements.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
